question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Momentum toward a 10-year baseline under Earned Settlement is evident from official consultations and late-2025 announcements, suggesting the policy direction is real and concrete.
However, there are substantial downsides: no enacted primary legislation by May 2026, potential legal challenges, and political shifts could delay or derail the timetable.
Exemptions and route-specific adjustments could accelerate or mitigate some cases, but overall timing remains uncertain, justifying a calibrated probability around 0.65.

justification.critique_assessment: Valid: objections identify genuine obstacles to enactment by May 2026 (legislation, lawsuits, political shifts) that plausibly reduce the odds from the stated ensemble.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from the ensemble 0.93 to 0.65 to account for the significant legislative and political uncertainties by May 2026; while there is plausible near-term movement (potential April 2026 implementation), it is not guaranteed.

forecasts.reference-class: Earned settlement policy proposals by the UK government to raise the baseline settlement waiting period to 10 years, with potential reductions for certain contributions or circumstances.

sources.claim: The consultation states the default qualifying period for settlement will be increased to ten years, with opportunities to reduce this period based on contributions.
The government announced that the baseline waiting period for many migrants would be ten years, though some groups could qualify sooner and others later, following the 2025 proposals.
Analyses indicate the standard waiting period would increase from five to ten years, with important exceptions depending on route and circumstances.
The immigration white paper proposes that the wait for settlement will double from 5 to 10 years, with various exemptions.
The government published a consultation proposing an 'earned settlement' model with a default 10-year qualifying period for settlement, plus a time-adjustment based on contribution.
House of Commons Library notes that the government announced details of the earned settlement proposal in November 2025, with a baseline of 10 years and exceptions.
The long-residence route already uses a 10-year qualifying period for settlement; time spent under different permissions can count toward the 10-year requirement.
IPPR warns that up to around 300,000 children could face a 10-year wait for settled status under proposed changes.
FT reports Reform UK's proposals to crack down on settlement, including longer residency periods and stricter criteria.

The government announced details of the proposal to raise the baseline qualifying period for settlement to ten years on 20 November 2025; some would qualify sooner while others would take longer; no changes enacted yet.
House of Commons Library briefing notes that the white paper proposes changing the 5-year baseline to 10 years for indefinite leave to remain, with exemptions.
Long residence rules require at least 10 years continuous lawful presence for settlement.
Guidance indicates the 10-year qualifying period applies to settlement via continuous residence rules.
The government proposed to extend the waiting period for permanent settlement from five to ten years in the immigration white paper.
